_comment: Spoken-line manifest for The Late Market. Source of truth for the Friday bake. Every entry mirrors a deps.say() call site exactly — `text` is the DISPLAY text (what the player reads); spokenText defaults to text (no acting tags in v1 so word-level alignment stays clean). `variants` expands template placeholders into baked line ids. Runtime lookup is by normalized display text.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: I'm Siki — I keep your books. That's Zana — she chases what's owed. £2,400 of yours is already sleeping out on that street.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: I'm Zana. You point, I chase. First one's Harborne — say the word.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: The shutters were left open. Day {day} of 3 — the books remember where you stopped.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: The Claims Desk in the market buys settling. They open every negotiation with their number. Notice whose number is already on the table.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Collector at the end of the row. Careful — he buys the customer with the debt.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Three runs. One invoice. Did your minimum move with their opening?

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: You never named a floor. Name it before their number arrives.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Mareline. Three years a customer, sixty days late, four times a year. Now silence.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Word travels. Two offers found your door already.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Look at what you paid while nobody answered.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: History is a fact. It is not a reason.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Market close. This is the street your decisions built.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Finally — the ledger the street keeps.

lines.speaker: factor
lines.text: Aged on your desk, did it? Good. I will pay you for the days you lost — the rest is mine.

lines.speaker: collector
lines.text: I buy the customer with the debt still on it. You keep the invoice; I keep the account.

lines.speaker: shark
lines.text: A little cash now, a little back each day. The daily number is small on purpose. Is it not?

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: There it is — the full face, on your till, not the street's.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Nobody owns a piece of your week now. Quayline is paid.

lines.speaker: collector
lines.text: First sitting. The desk slides a number across — no greeting. Numbers first.

lines.speaker: collector
lines.text: Second sitting. A different number. Same desk, same silence.

lines.speaker: collector
lines.text: Last sitting. The desk slides its final number across.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Still no reply. The line of credit is £60 open on the shelf, and doing nothing has to travel somewhere.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Still silence. The shelf keeps score.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Third knock, nothing. Decide what the silence is worth.

lines.speaker: factor
lines.text: No waiting. Today’s money, today — that is the whole of my offer.

lines.speaker: shark
lines.text: A little now. A little each day. The daily number is small — that is rather the point.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Chapter Two. The Offer. Everyone names a price first — except you.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Chapter Three. Good money after bad. The street remembers what you already spent.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: The week closes. Let's see what your patience was worth.

lines.speaker: shark
lines.text: That old debt of yours — the one from before your week. I'll take it off your hands. 70% of face, settled off the books.

lines.speaker: shark
lines.text: Pleasure doing business. The street thanks you — literally.

lines.speaker: shark
lines.text: Your loss. The street keeps its own books.

lines.speaker: shark
lines.text: Eighty-five? Cute. Seventy, off the books, tonight — or nothing.

lines.speaker: factor
lines.text: You look like someone who'd rather have it today.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: سوقان. أسبوع واحد. قانونان مختلفان.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: السوق. الأسبوع نفسه، لكن قانون مختلف — شروطك أنت تحدد ثمن التأخير، والزكاة تنتظر ما لا تحصّله أبدًا.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: والسوق يحتفظ بدفتر آخر: الزكاة على ما لا يزال مستحقًا لك. اثنان ونصف بالمئة — مستحقة سواء سُدِّدت الفاتورة أم لا.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: اليوم الأول. الخزينة فيها 5,760 درهمًا. فاتورة كوايلين البالغة 9,600 درهم تستحق في اليوم الرابع. هناك شيء في الدفتر ينزف بالفعل.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: مكتب التسوية في السوق يشتري الاتفاق. يفتحون كل تفاوض برقمهم. لاحظ أي رقم صار على الطاولة بالفعل.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: ماريلاين. ثلاث سنوات كعميلة، متأخرة ستون يومًا، أربع مرات في السنة. والآن صمت.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: ظلت الزكاة تتراكم على ما لم تحصّله طوال الأسبوع. السوق يحسب ما نسيه الصندوق.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: إغلاق السوق. هذا هو الشارع الذي بنتْه قراراتك.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Harborne is already late. Chase it, or leave it for the street.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Quayline's bill is due today. Pay it, or the street starts charging.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Harborne again. Same amount. This one lands after the week closes.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Heads up. Shark about — walk past him.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: That money is still on the street.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Nothing you were owed is still sitting out.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: You deferred one and chased the other. The offers matched. Only when the money landed changed. That tilt is present bias.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: You chased both. The near one and the far one were the same offer.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: You left both. The near one and the far one were the same offer. That tilt is present bias.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Your week in one line: a clean ledger — nothing leaned on you this week.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Run it back and see if it holds.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Your week in one line: their opening number moved your bottom line more than the law did.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Quote the Act first. Open with your number, not theirs.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Your week in one line: their opening number moved your bottom line more than your own terms did.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Open with your number, and the fee you wrote into the terms.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Your week in one line: the history kept charging you after the prospect stopped paying.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Decide at zero. Judge the old account like a fresh one.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Your week in one line: the near cost always shouted loudest, and the far one barely whispered.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Chase Tuesday's money on Tuesday.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Your floor moved. The invoice never did. That is anchoring.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: I'm Siki — I keep your books. That's Zana — she chases what's owed. AED 11,520 of yours is already sleeping out on that street.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: The street keeps its books whether you open or not. Yours begin the moment you open the shutters.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Harborne has the money. It chose not to hand it over. Go and get it.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Chasing isn't rude — the law agrees. A late commercial invoice earns statutory interest from day one: base rate plus eight.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Pay the bill. Or tomorrow I read you the late fee — louder.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Parliament priced lateness in 1998: forty pounds fixed, plus interest at base plus eight. The street charges more, and calls it a favour.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: Same invoice as day one. What you do today says who you are — not the weather.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Identical numbers. One difference: when the money lands. Watch what your gut does with later.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: That's the first stall you lit. £2,400 sleeps out there tonight — it doesn't come home by itself.

lines.speaker: collector
lines.text: I heard the street charging you. When you'd rather sell the account than keep the chase — I'm at the end of the row.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: That shadow crossing the stalls — him. He prices patience, and he hasn't forgotten you kept yours.

lines.speaker: zana
lines.text: He came back with a new number — seventy-eight, up from seventy. Clean books cost him profit. That's your discipline, priced by the street.

lines.speaker: siki
lines.text: Breathe. Still saveable, in order: what's owed to you, then what you owe. The street only wins the days you give it.
